newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee keeps modest gains by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee keeps modest gains by close.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures kept modest gains by the close on Wednesday on scale-down manufacturer buying after Asian selling dried up, traders said.
"There was a bit of Far East selling but this was taken out," said one.
Benchmark September was traded between $1,805 and $1,835 before closing $39 up at $1,824, the middle of the range.
Volume at 3,294 lots was tiny and dominated by the September position.
Technically, analysts said the market was likely to continue base-building following the recent sharp downward move, before attempting another rally.

On the upside, the $2,000 level basis September was seen more as a psychological barrier than anything else. The last time the contract held above $2,000 was on June 10 and well below the twin peaks of $2,700 in late May.
New York arabica futures continued to stay up by midsession on chart-driven speculative buying.
U.S. traders said the market continued to derive strength from an USDA attache report for the 1997/98 Brazil crop.

The attache report, dated May 9, put Brazil's 1997/98 harvest at 24 million 60-kg bags, down sharply from the USDA's official Brazil estimate of 28 million bags published in its 1997/98 world coffee production report in June.
Several European traders on Wednesday asked the USDA to clear the air over the conflicting figures.
On the physical front, traders said business in Europe has dried up up due to the summer lull and the tight Asian and Central American supplies.
